prompt:
A company has three funnels. Enterprise: 2,000 visitors with lead, demo, and close rates of 30%, 40%, and 25%. SMB: 5,000 visitors with rates 20%, 30%, and 20%. Self-serve: 8,000 visitors with rates 15%, 25%, and 16%. Choose any interventions within 7 budget units: A costs 4 and adds 5 percentage points to Enterprise lead rate and 2 points to SMB lead rate; B costs 3 and adds 5 points to every demo rate; C costs 5 and adds 3 points to Enterprise close rate and 4 points to both other close rates; D costs 2 and adds 1,000 Self-serve visitors at the unchanged Self-serve rates. Effects of selected interventions combine, and expected closes equal visitors times all three stage rates. What is 100 times the maximum expected total closes?

Solve the problem. End your response with a final line containing only the numeric answer.

An experiment has three preregistered strata with population weights 50%, 30%, and 20%. In New customers, control-assigned conversion is 4%, treatment-assigned conversion is 5.2%, treatment take-up is 80% among treatment-assigned and 20% among control-assigned. In Returning, the four figures are 10%, 11.5%, 75%, and 25%. In Enterprise, they are 20%, 21%, 60%, and 10%. Within each stratum, estimate the local average treatment effect for compliers using the Wald adjustment: divide the treatment-minus-control conversion-rate difference by the treatment-minus-control take-up difference. Then population-weight the three effects. How many incremental conversions does the result imply per 10,000 customers?

Solve the problem. End your response with a final line containing only the numeric answer.

A campaign market had 1,000 pre-period sales and 1,450 post-period sales. A synthetic control uses donor growth-factor weights 50%, 30%, and 20%; the donors' observed post/pre growth factors are 1.10, 1.20, and 0.95. Campaign spillover reduced every donor's observed growth factor by exactly 0.02, so correct each donor factor upward by 0.02 before combining them. Only 80% of eligible customers in the campaign market were actually reached. Assuming unreached customers had zero effect and effect scales linearly with reach, what is the implied incremental sales at 100% reach?

Solve the problem. End your response with a final line containing only the numeric answer.

Four channels A, B, C, and D have coalition conversion values v: v(∅)=0; v(A)=18, v(B)=12, v(C)=9, v(D)=5; v(AB)=38, v(AC)=31, v(AD)=25, v(BC)=26, v(BD)=19, v(CD)=20; v(ABC)=60, v(ABD)=51, v(ACD)=46, v(BCD)=42; v(ABCD)=80. Compute channel B's four-player Shapley value, using every ordering of the channels as equally likely. What is six times B's Shapley value?

Solve the problem. End your response with a final line containing only the numeric answer.

Choose Basic price b from {40,50,60} dollars and Pro price p from {100,120,140} dollars, subject to p being at least twice b. Demand is D_B=2600−30b+3(p−100) Basic units and D_P=1300−8p+3(b−40) Pro units. Unit costs are $20 for Basic and $60 for Pro. There are no fixed costs. What is the maximum contribution profit (b−20)D_B+(p−60)D_P in dollars?

Solve the problem. End your response with a final line containing only the numeric answer.

Audience weights are Enterprise 50, SMB 30, and Developer 20. Six claims have (Enterprise,SMB,Developer) scores and production costs: A=(9,5,4), cost 4; B=(7,9,5), cost 3; C=(5,7,10), cost 3; D=(3,9,8), cost 2; E=(10,4,6), cost 4; F=(6,6,9), cost 2. A claim's base impact is 50×Enterprise score+30×SMB score+20×Developer score. Select exactly three claims with total cost at most 9. A and E cannot both be selected; D requires B. Pair B+C incurs an 80-point overlap penalty; C+F adds a 90-point synergy; A+F adds a 50-point synergy; all other pair adjustments are zero. What is the maximum total impact?

Solve the problem. End your response with a final line containing only the numeric answer.

A budget has 10 units. Successive blocks in each channel must be bought in order. Search blocks cost 2 each and yield 90, 70, and 50 conversions; Social blocks cost 2 each and yield 75, 60, and 40; Email blocks cost 1 each and yield 45 and 35; Video blocks cost 3 each and yield 100 and 75; Affiliate blocks cost 1 each and yield 40 and 30. Buying any Video block requires at least one Social block. Buying the second Affiliate block requires at least one Search block. Having at least one Search and one Email block adds 20 conversions; having at least one Social and one Video block adds 30. What is the maximum total conversions within budget?

Solve the problem. End your response with a final line containing only the numeric answer.

Choose at most one localization level per market. Each option lists engineering units, translation units, and monthly incremental contribution in local currency: Taiwan Basic=(1,2,NT$90,000), Full=(2,4,NT$156,000); Japan Basic=(1,3,¥375,000), Full=(3,5,¥825,000); Germany Basic=(2,2,€3,360), Full=(4,3,€5,760); Brazil Basic=(1,2,R$14,000), Full=(2,4,R$25,000). Budgets are 6 engineering and 9 translation units, and at most three markets may be selected. Select at least one of Taiwan/Japan and at least one of Germany/Brazil. Japan Full requires at least Taiwan Basic. Germany Full and Brazil Full cannot both be selected. Use US$1=NT$30=¥150, US$1=€0.80, and US$1=R$5. What is the maximum monthly incremental contribution in US dollars?

Solve the problem. End your response with a final line containing only the numeric answer.
